legend: You are playing an online game, you have a team of N$$$N$$$ players, and you decided to challenge your friend's team that also consists of N$$$N$$$ players, let's call them team A$$$A$$$ and team B$$$B$$$ respectively. Each player has a specific strength, more specifically the ith$$$i_{th}$$$ player in team A$$$A$$$ has strength equal to i$$$i$$$ for each i$$$i$$$ between 1$$$1$$$ and N$$$N$$$, and the jth$$$j_{th}$$$ player from team B$$$B$$$ has strength equal to j+1$$$j+1$$$ for each j$$$j$$$ between 1$$$1$$$ and N$$$N$$$.

The total strength of a team is the product of strengths of all players in the team. To make the game fair, you can swap the ith$$$i_{th}$$$ player from team A$$$A$$$ with the ith$$$i_{th}$$$ player from team B$$$B$$$ for any i$$$i$$$ between 1$$$1$$$ and N$$$N$$$, in other words, you can only swap players that have the same index in both teams. You can repeat the previous operation any number of times.
A game is fair when both of the teams have a equal strengths. Can you make the game fair?
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases T$$$T$$$ (1≤T≤105$$$1 \le T \le 10^5$$$). Description of the test cases follows.
Each of the following T$$$T$$$ lines, contains a single integer N$$$N$$$ (1≤N≤105$$$1\le{N}\le{10}^5$$$).
output: For each test case, if you can make the game fair then print in one line an integer M$$$M$$$,the total number of operations needed, on the next line print M$$$M$$$ (1≤M≤N$$$ 1 \le M \le N$$$) distinct integers, the indices where you want to apply the swap operation. If you can't make the game fair, then print in one line the value −1$$$-1$$$.
Note that you don't have to minimize the total number of operations. If there exists more than one answer print any of them.
